blocks.x: There is a plain version of smart contract engineering & audit: Contracts as production software — specification, formal verification and audit before value moves. We run it with named gates, signed baselines and a weekly evidence cadence — the details are below, in the order they happen.
What we deliver under this name

Smart contracts hold real value and fail expensively; we treat them as production software with a safety culture. Delivery starts with specification: state machines, invariants and failure modes written down and reviewed with the business before code. Implementation follows patterns with known properties (upgradeability chosen deliberately, access control explicit, reentrancy and oracle risks engineered out), verified with static analysis, property-based fuzzing and — where stakes justify — formal verification of core invariants.

Audit is a stage, not a rubber stamp: independent review by specialists separate from the build team, findings triaged by severity, fixes re-tested, and a public (or supervisory) audit trail. Post-deployment, monitoring watches for anomalous state transitions, and incident runbooks pre-define pause procedures — because the ability to stop safely is a feature, not an admission.

The sectors where Smart Contract Engineering & Audit currently runs: Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Logistics & Supply Chain, Energy & Utilities. Each engagement anchors to one named metric in that sector's own language.
